content_sections.heading: About GeM
content_sections.text: Government eMarketplace is a Government Company registered under Section 8 of the Companies Act, under the Ministry of Commerce & Industry, Government of India. It is a single digital platform that government departments, organisations and PSUs use to buy goods and services from sellers across India. It covers the whole process, from vendor registration and item selection to delivery and payment.

content_sections.heading: GeM Manager (Buyer Management- MoD and MHA) Eligibility 2026
content_sections.text: Eligibility is judged as on the last date for receiving applications, which is 8 November 2026. GeM's selection committee may relax or extend the eligibility criteria and educational qualifications. Essential: Graduate Degree in any discipline from a recognized University Desirable: Post Graduate degree in any discipline from a recognized university Essential: At least 11 years of experience in business development, key account management or a similar role. Preferable: A strong understanding of Government procurement processes. Preferable: Knowledge of GFR, DoE procurement guidelines and the GeM procurement framework. Preferable: Ability to analyse procurement cases and provide practical solutions. Strong people management, relationship management and leadership skills Capability to work in a fast-paced, high-growth environment Result oriented, with a high bias for action and sharp business acumen Empathetic, positive attitude and a desire to help clients progress towards their goals Ability to influence decision making for win-win results High on ownership and self-motivation Knowledge of MS Office (PowerPoint and Excel) Ability to perform data analytics and generate reports using a BI Tool Proficient in handling confidential and restricted communications Ability to analyze tenders and prepare detailed reports Strong verbal and written communication skills Before applying, check the full eligibility for the post in the official notification.

content_sections.heading: Role and Responsibilities
content_sections.text: The Manager is the single point of contact (SPoC) for Defence (MoD) and MHA organisations and their buyers and consignees on GeM. The duties are listed under these heads: Buyer Management: help these organisations get onboarded, build their capacity and use GeM well. Track procurement trends and GeM adoption, and work with the relevant GeM verticals to resolve systemic issues. Procurement and Policy Advisory: examine cases against GFR, GeM GTC, DoE Manuals, DPM and other applicable Government rules. Advise on procurement modes such as Category, Bid, RA, Custom Bid/BOQ and PAC/STE/LTE, and recommend Defence-specific clarifications. Integration and Stakeholder Management: coordinate with MoD and MHA organisations, engage with senior officials, and prepare briefs, presentations, notes, ATRs and inputs for leadership. Procurement Case Examination: handle complex cases involving technical or financial evaluation, RA/L1, MSE/MII, post-bid changes, price matching, quantity distribution, contract amendments or cancellation, and EPBG/performance security. Recommendations must be documented and defensible. Monitoring and Performance Management: track GMV, orders, buyer participation, savings and other KPIs, ministry by ministry. Prepare dashboards, MIS and briefs, and monitor high-value procurements. Policy, Process and System Improvement: work with the Product, Technology, Policy, Category, Legal and other verticals. Support Defence-relevant GeM functions and collect structured feedback from users. Capacity Building and Outreach: run buyer workshops, training programmes, buyer meets and awareness sessions. Write advisories, FAQs and guidance notes, and support Defence-specific campaigns. Issue Resolution and Escalation: act as the escalation point for critical buyer issues, keep records of decisions, and escalate systemic or policy matters with clear recommendations. Key Shared Accountabilities: work with the tech and customer experience teams to communicate MoD and MHA buyer needs, for example integrated payment systems and value-added services.

content_sections.heading: Selection Process
content_sections.text: GeM may shortlist candidates for an interview. Meeting the minimum eligibility does not guarantee a place on the interview shortlist. GeM will not take part in any correspondence about selection, and its decisions are final in all matters.

content_sections.heading: Service Conditions
content_sections.text: The engagement is contractual, under GeM's Project Management Unit (PMU). The initial period is 5 years. It can be extended depending on performance and GeM's needs. The place of posting is New Delhi.

faq.question: Q1. How many years of experience does the GeM Manager post require?
faq.answer: You need at least 11 years of experience in business development, key account management or a similar role. The application form asks you to confirm this directly.

faq.question: Q2. Is a post-graduate degree compulsory?
faq.answer: No. A Graduate Degree in any discipline is the essential qualification. A Post Graduate degree in any discipline is only desirable.

faq.question: Q3. Is this a permanent job?
faq.answer: No. It is a contractual engagement under GeM's Project Management Unit (PMU) for an initial period of 5 years. It can be extended depending on performance and GeM's needs.

faq.question: Q4. Where will the selected candidate work?
faq.answer: The job is in New Delhi. The application form asks whether you are open to working in Delhi.

faq.question: Q5. What must the application email contain?
faq.answer: It must contain your updated CV and your answers to the application form questions, including your current and expected annual CTC and how soon you can join. Applications without the form will not be considered.

faq.question: Q6. Which procurement rules should a candidate know?
faq.answer: Knowledge of GFR, DoE procurement guidelines and the GeM procurement framework is preferred. The duties also involve checking cases against GeM GTC, DoE Manuals and DPM.

faq.question: Q7. Will every eligible applicant be called for an interview?
faq.answer: No. GeM may shortlist candidates for an interview, and meeting the minimum eligibility does not guarantee a place on the shortlist.

faq.question: Q8. Which date is used to check eligibility?
faq.answer: The last date for receiving applications, 8 November 2026, is the crucial date for deciding eligibility.

faq.question: Q9. Which software skills does the post need?
faq.answer: The required skills include MS Office (PowerPoint and Excel) and the ability to analyse data and generate reports using a BI Tool.
